thread:
harper: heads-up: invoice-preview shows a small but persistent duplicate token bump (~200 tokens) for several tenants after a kafka partition rebalance around 04:10 UTC. saw it in canary and prod sample.
leo: interesting, duplicates after rebalance usually mean exactly-once path broke. do we have logs for re-emits?
harper: yes — two emits for same req_id within 2s with different kafka offsets.
```
2024-10-09T04:09:59Z INFO emitter publish tenant=T-12 req=REQ-77 offset=12045
2024-10-09T04:10:00Z INFO emitter publish tenant=T-12 req=REQ-77 offset=12400 (rebalance replay)
```

tess: aggregator is supposed to dedupe on (tenant, req_id, source_epoch). looks like source_epoch changed during replay. we probably treat replayed messages as new.
leo: pipeline currently uses kafka offset -> epoch mapping to decide canonical emission. during rebalance the emitter rewrites epoch tags which breaks idempotency.
harper: short-term fix: have aggregator dedupe purely on (tenant, req_id) for a 30s tail window regardless of epoch, and emit a telemetry counter `metering.rebalance_deduped`. this is conservative but will stop the invoice bump.
tess: cautious: pure (tenant, req_id) dedupe might suppress legit repeated requests if a client retried legitimately within 30s. but retries usually include an Idempotency-Key we can prefer. maybe dedupe order: Idempotency-Key -> req_id -> fingerprint.
leo: agree: implement (1) prefer Idempotency-Key if present, (2) fallback to req_id with 30s grace during rebalance signals, (3) increase debug logging for rebalance windows. Also add an alert if `metering.rebalance_deduped` > 5/min for any tenant.
ops-bot: plan: deploy aggregator hotfix to canary in 15m, monitor invoice-preview deltas for 1h.
metering-bot: NOTICE: aggregator flagged 12 dedupes in last 5m for canary.
harper: i'm going to PR the canary patch now (AGG-2045). follow-up: file a producer ticket to preserve epoch tags across rebalance and add a checkpointing layer so emitter doesn't re-publish already-ack'd events.
tess: good. also add a small reconciler job to correct the handful of previews affected over last 24h once patch is staged.
leo: ok thanks. closing when canary is stable and recon completes. :thumbsup:
